title: Iran Attaches Four-to-Five-Day Deadline to Ceasefire Roadmap as Trump Refuses to Lift Blockade First
detail: Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei attached a clock to Iran's Sept 23 ceasefire roadmap, warning Washington has four to five days — expiring around Sept 28-29 — to respond. Trump acknowledged 'momentum towards a deal' but ruled out lifting the naval blockade before Iran demonstrates sufficient goodwill, the core sticking point since Iran's roadmap lifts the blockade inside the ceasefire while Washington wants Iranian steps first. In a separate UNGA address, Pezeshkian vowed Iran would never 'bend at the knee' and warned Iran would expand the war into the Indian Ocean if the US attacks again, while reiterating Iran does not seek nuclear weapons but claims the right to peaceful nuclear technology.

media.caption: Iran attaches a four-to-five-day deadline to its ceasefire roadmap as Trump declines to lift the Hormuz blockade first

title: Dozens of Delegations Walk Out as Netanyahu Addresses UN; Iran Calls It 'a Loudspeaker for Justifying War'
detail: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's UN General Assembly address triggered a mass walkout by scores of delegations, leaving many seats empty; Netanyahu responded by calling those who left 'moral cowards' and said the decision to attack Iran 'was one of the easiest decisions I've ever had to make.' Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Netanyahu 'came to the General Assembly to turn the podium of this international institution into a loudspeaker for justifying war and aggression; but the exit of 77 delegations from the hall spoke louder than any speech,' adding that 'history will judge the crimes, occupation, and aggression, not the publicity stunts in New York.'

media.caption: Delegates walk out of the UN General Assembly hall as Netanyahu begins his address

title: Senior IRGC Commander Hossein Zarifi Killed in Clash With Gunmen in Southeastern Iran
detail: Brig.-Gen. Hossein Zarifi, commander of the IRGC's Shahid Sajjad Operational Headquarters in Saravan, was killed in a clash with an armed cell in the Jihadabad area of Saravan, Sistan and Baluchestan province, near the Pakistan border. The IRGC Ground Forces' Quds Regional Headquarters said a joint IRGC-Intelligence Ministry-police raid targeted a group it described as planning an attack; five members of the cell were killed and others arrested in the ensuing exchange of fire. No group has claimed responsibility. Zarifi had served in the province for over a decade; his funeral was held in Saravan on Sept 25.

media.caption: IRGC Brig.-Gen. Hossein Zarifi, killed in a clash with an armed cell in Saravan

title: Pezeshkian Tells Fox News Iran Will Dilute 60%-Enriched Uranium, Accept Verification
detail: In an interview with Fox News' Bret Baier, President Masoud Pezeshkian denied Iran seeks nuclear weapons — 'Not at all... it is unholy, it is illegal' — and offered to dilute Iran's stockpile of uranium enriched to 60% and submit to international verification: 'We said we're willing to dilute them. It's not a big deal... They can have free access to see whatever we have.' He pointed to the collapsed June MOU with Trump as the basis to move forward. The offer drew immediate hardline domestic backlash: activist Mohammad-Hossein Chavoshi told Pezeshkian to stop 'spout[ing] nonsense about nuclear matters,' and hardline MP Amir-Hossein Sabeti filed an impeachment motion against Foreign Minister Araghchi. IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi and Mashhad prayer leader Ahmad Alamolhoda separately warned of Iran's capacity to escalate if US pressure continues.

media.caption: Iran's President Pezeshkian tells Fox News Iran is willing to dilute enriched uranium and accept verification
